- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast 3–5 days post-spike at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.0 units per day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0 units; if <1.5σ below, increase by 0.5–1.0 units.
- Sentiment history with high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00) correlates with model lagging 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged true values.
